summary.headline: Gravita Q1 FY27 revenue rose 42% YoY to INR1,475 crore and PAT 14% to INR106.39 crore, but lead volumes fell on Gulf supply disruption.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 42% YoY to INR1,475 crore, adjusted EBITDA rose 29% to INR145 crore (margin over 9.8%), and PAT rose 14% to INR106.39 crore, with total volumes up only 4% to 55,455 MT. Lead volumes declined YoY because Middle East war disruptions cut scrap imports, with 15-20% of imports routed via the Gulf. The copper subsidiary (Rashtriya Metal Industries) ran at 50% utilisation and contributed INR376 crore revenue. Management guided that copper plus a higher value-added mix (63% of revenue) will drive growth while lead margins are protected, and that the Phagi lead expansion of 40,500 MT was commissioned with INR30 crore of internal accruals.

financial_highlights.metric: EBITDA per ton: lead / aluminium / plastic / copper

financial_highlights.change: raised by copper inventory and goods in transit

financial_highlights.value: INR47 crore (INR35 crore operational, INR13 crore non-operational)

segments.name: Lead
segments.commentary: Volumes fell YoY due to scrap shortage from Gulf disruption; Mundra expansion ran at about 50% utilisation and Phagi (Jaipur) at about 45%. Management guided similar EBITDA margins for lead next quarter despite lower top-line.

segments.name: Copper (Rashtriya Metal Industries subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Ran at 50% utilisation, contributing INR376 crore revenue and EBITDA of about INR55,151 per ton. Management expects about 60%+ utilisation by year-end, with a 29,400 MT Gujarat copper plant (INR160 crore capex) due within 12 months.

segments.name: Aluminium and plastic
segments.commentary: Q1 per-ton EBITDA of INR25,175 (aluminium) and INR10,197 (plastic) included price gains; management's sustainable range is INR15-17/kg aluminium (overseas operations) and INR10-12/kg plastic.

guidance_outlook: Lead volumes likely to stay under pressure in Q2 FY27 from Gulf logistics; management expects lead EBITDA margins similar to Q1.
Copper EBITDA per ton expected to stay around INR55,000 near term, rising to about INR60,000 by year-end and INR65,000-75,000 over 2-3 years.

Copper capacity to double to about 60,000 MT per annum within 3 years; Phagi and Gujarat lead capacity expected to reach about 70% utilisation once scrap normalises, with about INR50 crore extra monthly revenue at optimal utilisation.
Installed capacity 4.97 lakh MT per annum; target over 8 lakh MT per annum by FY29. Total capex of INR1,680 crore through FY29, of which INR850 crore for existing businesses.
Management reiterated PAT growth target of 25-30% CAGR and copper business ROCE reaching about 25% in roughly 2.5-3 years; group ROCE currently about 20%.
capex_capacity: Phagi (Jaipur) lead plant expanded by 40,500 MT per annum at about INR30 crore, funded internally; total plant capacity now 75,819 MT per annum.
Copper: 29,400 MT per annum recycling plant in Gujarat, estimated INR160 crore, on track for commissioning within 12 months; bottleneck debottlenecking expected to finish by end of FY27.
Rubber capacity (Eastern Europe plant machinery) put on hold; copper expansion fast-tracked in that area.
Kathua manufacturing unit operations to be consolidated into Jaipur.
Own scrap yards being set up in the US and developed economies for copper, lead, aluminium and plastic, to be in place by end of FY27.
demand_pricing: Scrap shortage in India and demand-supply mismatch let management lift lead margins despite lower volumes.

Copper alloy realisations priced off monthly or fortnightly LME averages and hedged metal-by-metal (e.g. 70% copper / 30% zinc for brass); management said Gravita remains 100% hedged, so copper price rises do not flow through to profit.
Average LME copper about $13,500/t in Q1 FY27 versus about $9,000 a year earlier, diluting margin percentage.
Domestic sourcing about 35% for India plants.
Lead brand GRAVITA M listed on the London Metal Exchange (lead from Mundra); management said no LME sales yet, and the listing is aimed at new OEM approvals.
MCX inclusion of ADC12 aluminium alloy still pending with the exchange; management expects it within this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did lead volumes decline YoY, and what is the FY27/FY28 lead volume outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed Middle East war supply disruption; 15-20% of imports come via the Gulf. Volume guidance was not given; growth is expected from copper and the Phagi/Mundra expansion once scrap normalises.

qa_highlights.question: When will copper reach 100% utilisation and how does margin bridge from 5.2% vs about 8% last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is at 50%, expected 60%+ by year-end; EBITDA per ton is seen at about INR55,000 with gradual increases. Management said last year's margin included copper price gains and that the margin percentage is diluted by higher LME prices.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt and working capital cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt is close to INR150 crore; working capital cycle is about 95 days, higher due to copper inventory and goods in transit.

qa_highlights.question: Plastic and aluminium sustainable EBITDA per kg?
qa_highlights.answer: Plastic sustainable INR10-12/kg; aluminium INR15-17/kg when only overseas operations run (INR13-14 when Indian operations run). Q1 figures included price gains.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company setting up its own copper yards and is there a cost impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is moving away from arbitrage agents to its own yards in developed economies (US), which it expects to lower procurement cost; lead yards were not viable earlier at lead-only scale.

qa_highlights.question: What is Mundra's new lead capacity utilisation, and is pyrolysis oil replacement contributing?
qa_highlights.answer: Mundra ran at about 50% including the February expansion; management said pyrolysis oil was already in use at Mundra and the Eastern European plant is not supplying India.

qa_highlights.question: Is ROCE below 20%, and where is it heading?
qa_highlights.answer: ROCE is about 20% currently, held back by lead capacity under-utilisation and copper premium paid on acquisition; management expects a rise toward 25% over about 3 years.

risks_watch: Lead volume recovery depends on Gulf logistics normalising; 15-20% of scrap imports routed via the Gulf, and management expects some impact in Q2 FY27 too.
Copper utilisation at 50% in Q1 with a target of 60%+ by year-end; ramp depends on debottlenecking completing by end-FY27 and EBITDA per ton holding near INR55,000.
Working capital cycle near 95 days and net debt near INR150 crore, both raised by copper inventory and goods in transit.
Group ROCE about 20% is held back by lead under-utilisation and the premium paid for the copper acquisition; management targets about 25% in 2.5-3 years.
Other income of INR47 crore includes INR35 crore operational income tied to hedging gains and losses, so its sustainability is uncertain.
Pending MCX listing of ADC12 aluminium alloy, with management expecting it within this year but MCX holding the decision.
Execution on the 29,400 MT Gujarat copper plant (INR160 crore) and on the own scrap yards in the US and developed economies, both due by end-FY27.
key_quotes: So there was a little decline in the volumes of lead, which was primarily because of supply chain disruptions because of this Middle East war .

So it's extremely difficult to talk about on a division -wise volume growth, especially in a very short-term period because, as I mentioned, there is some disruption, which is still not back to normal.
But because Gravita remains 100% hedged, so generally, you would not see certain upsides from copper commodity increase in Gravita.
So inventory value is close to INR1,040 crores, which is almost similar at March level, March '26 level.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on long-term growth and the copper and capacity pipeline, but cautious and somewhat evasive on near-term lead volumes and division-wise volume guidance, which it declined to give. It repeatedly attributed the shortfall to Gulf supply disruption and framed the response as margin protection.

growth.why: Management guides PAT growth of 25-30% and copper utilisation rising to 60%+ by FY27 end plus a 29,400 MT Gujarat copper plant and copper doubling in 3 years, but lead volumes are down YoY on Gulf scrap disruption and group utilisation is only about 52%, so near-term growth is not yet backed by volumes.
